questions.question: What is the line of latitude at 0° called?
questions.explanation: The Equator divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

questions.question: Which mountain range separates France from Spain?
questions.explanation: The Pyrenees form much of the border.

questions.question: What is the capital of France?
questions.explanation: Paris has been the capital of France for centuries and sits on the river Seine.

questions.question: Which semi-arid belt lies just south of the Sahara and stretches across Africa?
questions.explanation: The Sahel is a transition zone between desert and savanna.

questions.question: Which seasonal wind pattern brings heavy summer rains to South Asia?
questions.explanation: The monsoon reverses direction between summer and winter.

questions.question: Which climate zone is warm and wet all year, found near the Equator?
questions.explanation: Rain falls nearly every day in places like the Amazon and Congo basins.

questions.question: On a standard Mercator world map Greenland looks about as big as Africa. About how many times larger is Africa in reality?
questions.explanation: Africa is about 30.4 million square km and Greenland about 2.2 million.
questions.misconception: Many people think Greenland is as large as Africa because it looks so on many maps.

questions.question: Which is the largest US state by area?
questions.explanation: Alaska covers about 1.7 million square kilometres, more than twice the size of Texas.

questions.question: Which country is made up of more than 17,000 islands?
questions.explanation: It is the world's largest archipelagic state.

questions.question: Which is the largest country in Oceania by area?
questions.explanation: Australia covers about 7.7 million square kilometres.

questions.question: Which of these countries has a capital that is NOT its largest city?
questions.explanation: Turkey's capital is Ankara, but Istanbul is larger. Paris, Tokyo and Bangkok are both capital and largest city.
questions.misconception: Many people think a country's capital is always its largest city.

questions.question: Which of these countries is NOT landlocked?
questions.explanation: Portugal has an Atlantic coast; the other three have no sea coast.
questions.misconception: Many people think any country far from the sea is as landlocked as any other.

questions.question: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara covers about 9 million square kilometres. Antarctica is the largest desert overall.

questions.question: How many Great Lakes are there in North America?
questions.explanation: Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie and Ontario make five.

questions.question: Which African waterfall, called "the smoke that thunders", lies on the Zambezi River?
questions.explanation: The local name Mosi-oa-Tunya means "the smoke that thunders".

questions.question: Niagara Falls lies on the border between the United States and which country?
questions.explanation: Niagara Falls is on the border between Ontario, in Canada, and New York State.

questions.question: Which is the highest mountain in the Alps?
questions.explanation: Mont Blanc is about 4,806 metres high.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific covers about a third of the planet's surface.

questions.question: Which line of latitude lies at about 23.5° north?
questions.explanation: It marks the northernmost latitude where the Sun can be directly overhead.

questions.question: Which continent is almost entirely covered by ice?
questions.explanation: Its ice sheet averages more than two kilometres thick.

questions.question: Which two rivers gave Mesopotamia its name, 'the land between the rivers'?
questions.explanation: Both rise in the highlands of Turkey.

questions.question: Which river flows through the centre of Paris?
questions.explanation: The Seine runs through Paris on its way to the English Channel.

questions.question: The Nile flows north into which sea?
questions.explanation: The river forms a large delta before reaching the Mediterranean.

questions.question: Which river flows through Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade?
questions.explanation: It crosses or borders ten countries.

questions.question: Which river flows through or along Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam?
questions.explanation: The Mekong is the great river of mainland Southeast Asia.

questions.question: Which great river runs through the desert from south to north and is the main source of water for Egypt?
questions.explanation: Almost all of Egypt's people live along the Nile and its delta.

questions.question: Which river is the longest in Asia?
questions.explanation: The Yangtze, in China, is the longest river in Asia and the third longest in the world.

questions.question: Which river, Africa's second longest, flows through the Congo rainforest?
questions.explanation: The Congo is about 4,700 km long and drains the world's second largest rainforest.

questions.question: Into which body of water does the Volga flow?
questions.explanation: The Volga, Europe's longest river, empties into the Caspian Sea.

questions.question: Which river is the main river of West Africa, flowing through Mali, Niger and Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Niger is West Africa's great river and gave its name to two countries.

questions.question: Which is the longest river in Australia?
questions.explanation: The Murray is Australia's longest river, at about 2,500 km.

questions.question: Which sea lies between southern Europe and North Africa?
questions.explanation: It is linked to the Atlantic by the Strait of Gibraltar.

questions.question: Mexico City stands at about what altitude above sea level?
questions.explanation: Mexico City lies on a high plateau, about 2,240 metres above sea level.

questions.question: About what share of Earth's land area does Russia cover?
questions.explanation: Russia covers about 17 million km² of Earth's roughly 149 million km² of land.

questions.question: Which country has 11 time zones on its mainland, the most on a single landmass?
questions.explanation: Russia spans 11 time zones, from Kaliningrad to Kamchatka.

questions.question: Which continent is the fifth largest by area, bigger than Europe?
questions.explanation: Antarctica covers about 14 million km² and Europe about 10 million km².

questions.question: About how big is Rhode Island?
questions.explanation: Rhode Island covers about 4,000 km², water included.

questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was purpose-built as the capital as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.explanation: Ottawa, in Ontario, has been Canada's capital since 1866.

questions.question: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.explanation: Brasília was inaugurated as the capital in 1960, replacing Rio de Janeiro.

questions.question: What is the capital of Turkey?
questions.explanation: Ankara became the capital in 1923. Istanbul is Turkey's largest city.

questions.question: What is the capital of New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Wellington, at the southern tip of the North Island, is the capital. Auckland is the largest city.

questions.question: Which major city is located on both sides of the Bosphorus, in Europe and in Asia?
questions.explanation: Istanbul straddles the Bosphorus strait, so part of it lies in each continent.

questions.question: Venice is built across a lagoon of roughly how many small islands?
questions.explanation: Venice stands on about 118 small islands, separated by canals.

questions.question: About what share of the Netherlands lies below sea level?
questions.explanation: Roughly a quarter of the country is below sea level, protected by dikes, dunes and pumps.

questions.question: Which is the busiest seaport in Europe by cargo handled?
questions.explanation: Rotterdam has led Europe's ports in cargo for decades, ahead of Antwerp-Bruges.

questions.question: Which city has the world's busiest container port?
questions.explanation: Shanghai has handled more containers than any other port for over a decade, around 49 million in 2023.

questions.question: Which strait, about 3 km wide at its narrowest, separates Sicily from mainland Italy?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Messina is about 3 kilometres wide at its narrowest point.

questions.question: Which is the largest city in Canada by population?
questions.explanation: Toronto is Canada's largest city. Ottawa, the capital, is much smaller.

questions.question: Which is the largest city in Brazil by population?
questions.explanation: São Paulo is by far Brazil's largest city. The capital, Brasília, is a planned city and much smaller.

questions.question: Which is the largest city in the United States by population?
questions.explanation: New York City, with more than eight million people, is far ahead of Los Angeles, which has about four million.

questions.question: Which is the largest city in Nigeria by population?
questions.explanation: Lagos is Nigeria's biggest city and its main port. Abuja, the capital, has been the seat of government since 1991.

questions.question: Roughly how many megacities, cities of 10 million people or more, exist in the world today?
questions.explanation: The United Nations counts around thirty megacities, and most of them are in Asia.

questions.question: Which is the largest city in New Zealand by population?
questions.explanation: Auckland has about 1.7 million people, far more than any other New Zealand city.

questions.question: Which of these cities has the most inhabitants in its urban area?
questions.explanation: Greater Tokyo is far larger than the other three, with more than 30 million people.

questions.question: Mawsynram in India is among the wettest places on Earth. About how much rain does it get in an average year?
questions.explanation: Mawsynram averages roughly 11 to 12 metres of rain a year, almost all of it in the monsoon.

questions.question: How many sovereign countries are there in Africa?
questions.explanation: Africa has 54 countries recognised by the United Nations, more than any other continent.

questions.question: Which continent has the most countries?
questions.explanation: Africa has 54 recognised sovereign states.

questions.question: Which is the smallest continent by land area?
questions.explanation: Australia/Oceania is the smallest, at about 8.5 million square kilometres.

questions.question: According to United Nations estimates since 2023, which country has the largest population?
questions.explanation: UN estimates indicated that India overtook China in 2023.

questions.question: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Vatican City covers only about 0.44 square kilometres.

questions.question: Which two South American countries are landlocked?
questions.explanation: Both lie inland.

questions.question: About how large is the Sahara?
questions.explanation: The Sahara covers roughly 9 million square kilometres, an area comparable to China or the United States.

questions.question: A desert is usually defined as getting less than about how much precipitation a year?
questions.explanation: Deserts get under about 250 mm of rain or snow a year, whatever their temperature.

questions.question: Which mountain range blocks moisture and helps keep the Atacama Desert so dry?
questions.explanation: The Andes wall off moist air from the east, and a cold current cools the coast, so rain almost never falls.

questions.question: Which South American desert is the driest non-polar desert on Earth?
questions.explanation: Some weather stations there have never recorded rain.

questions.question: About how far below sea level is Badwater Basin in Death Valley?
questions.explanation: Badwater Basin lies about 86 metres below sea level.

questions.question: About how high above sea level is La Paz, the world's highest capital city?
questions.explanation: La Paz stands at about 3,640 metres.

questions.question: About how high above sea level is the average ground in the Maldives?
questions.explanation: The average ground level in the Maldives is only about 1.5 metres.

questions.question: About how high is Antarctica on average?
questions.explanation: Counting its ice, Antarctica averages about 2,300 metres above sea level.

questions.question: Borneo is shared by how many countries?
questions.explanation: Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei share Borneo.

questions.question: Which channel separates Madagascar from mainland Africa?
questions.explanation: The Mozambique Channel is more than 400 km wide at its narrowest.

questions.question: About how many islands make up the Philippines?
questions.explanation: The Philippines counts roughly 7,600 islands, while neighbouring Indonesia has more than 17,000.

questions.question: Which is the second-largest island in Europe?
questions.explanation: Great Britain is first, Iceland second with about 103,000 km², and Ireland third with about 84,000 km².

questions.question: Which is the smallest island nation in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Nauru covers about 21 km².

questions.question: Which is the largest island in the world?
questions.explanation: Greenland covers about 2.17 million square kilometres. Australia is counted as a continent.

questions.question: About how high above sea level is Lake Titicaca?
questions.explanation: Lake Titicaca lies at about 3,800 metres.

questions.question: The Iguazu River, which makes the falls, is a tributary of which major river?
questions.explanation: The Iguazu River flows into the Parana.

questions.question: In which country is Lake Ladoga?
questions.explanation: Ladoga lies in north-western Russia.

questions.question: Why is the Great Salt Lake so salty?
choices: Seawater flows in from the Pacific
Water leaves it only by evaporation
questions.explanation: It has no outlet, so water leaves only by evaporation and the salt stays behind.

questions.question: Which continent has the most landlocked countries?
questions.explanation: Africa has 16 landlocked countries, Europe about 14 and Asia about 12.

questions.question: How many countries are completely surrounded by Italy?
questions.explanation: San Marino and Vatican City are both enclaves inside Italy.

questions.question: Alaska is about how many times bigger than Texas?
questions.explanation: Alaska covers about 1.7 million km² and Texas about 0.7 million km².

questions.question: Which of these countries is crossed by the Tropic of Capricorn?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Capricorn, at about 23.4° south, crosses Botswana, Namibia, South Africa and others.

questions.question: In the ideal system, how wide in longitude is each time zone?
questions.explanation: The Earth turns 360 degrees in 24 hours, so each hour of time equals 15 degrees of longitude.

questions.question: Mount Everest lies on the border of Nepal and which other country?
questions.explanation: The summit sits on the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.

questions.question: In which country is Mount Kilimanjaro?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest peak at 5,895 m, stands in northeastern Tanzania.

questions.question: China and which other country each border 14 countries, the most in the world?
questions.explanation: Both China and Russia have 14 land neighbours.

questions.question: Which tiny principality shares a land border only with France?
questions.explanation: Monaco is surrounded by France on land. Andorra borders both France and Spain.

questions.question: How many member states does the United Nations have?
questions.explanation: The United Nations has 193 member states. The Holy See and Palestine are observers.

questions.question: Which has more sovereign countries: South America or Oceania?
questions.explanation: Oceania has 14 sovereign countries and South America has 12.

questions.question: Brazil borders how many countries?
questions.explanation: It borders every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.

questions.question: Roughly what share of all the water on Earth is held in the oceans, rather than in ice, lakes, rivers or groundwater?
questions.explanation: Salt water in the oceans makes up about 97% of Earth's water. Fresh water is only about 3%.

questions.question: Which trench is the deepest part of the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Puerto Rico Trench, north of the island, reaches about 8.4 km at its deepest point, the Milwaukee Deep.

questions.question: The Pacific Ocean covers about what share of Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: At about 165 million km², the Pacific covers roughly a third of the planet, more than all the land put together.

questions.question: Water pressure rises by about one atmosphere for every how many metres of seawater?
questions.explanation: Every 10 m of seawater adds roughly one atmosphere of pressure.

questions.question: In which US state is North America's highest mountain?
questions.explanation: The highest peak in North America is in the Alaska Range.

questions.question: About how high is the highest mountain on mainland Australia?
questions.explanation: Mount Kosciuszko rises to about 2,230 metres.

questions.question: About how high is Mount Fuji?
questions.explanation: Mount Fuji is 3,776 metres high.

questions.question: About how high is the Matterhorn?
questions.explanation: The Matterhorn is 4,478 metres high.

questions.question: Most Ring of Fire volcanoes form at which kind of plate boundary?
questions.explanation: One plate sinks beneath another, melting rock that feeds volcanoes.

questions.question: Which two countries each have more than a billion inhabitants?
questions.explanation: Both exceed 1.4 billion.

questions.question: Which peninsula includes Norway and Sweden?
questions.explanation: It is the largest peninsula in Europe.

questions.question: Which river is traditionally considered the longest in Africa?
questions.explanation: The Nile, at roughly 6,650 km, is traditionally cited as the longest river in the world.

questions.question: Which river is the longest in South America?
questions.explanation: The Amazon is about 6,400 km long and carries more water than any other river.

questions.question: Which country contains the largest share of the Amazon rainforest?
questions.explanation: About 60 percent of the forest lies in Brazil.

questions.question: For part of its course the Rhine forms the border between which two countries?
questions.explanation: Between Basel and Karlsruhe the Rhine marks the French-German border.

questions.question: The Rio Grande flows into which body of water?
questions.explanation: The Rio Grande ends in the Gulf of Mexico.

questions.question: Through how many countries does the Euphrates flow?
questions.explanation: The Euphrates flows through Turkey, Syria and Iraq.

questions.question: Into which ocean does the Orange River flow?
questions.explanation: Unlike many South African rivers, the Orange flows west into the Atlantic.

questions.question: Which is the longest river on the Iberian Peninsula?
questions.explanation: The Tagus is about 1,000 km long, the longest river of the Iberian Peninsula.

questions.question: The Colorado River basin covers parts of how many US states?
questions.explanation: The basin covers parts of Wyoming, Colorado, Utah, New Mexico, Nevada, Arizona and California.

questions.question: Which river is the longest tributary of the Mississippi?
questions.explanation: The Missouri is the longest tributary, while the Ohio carries more water.

questions.question: The Yellow River gets its colour from what?
questions.explanation: The river carries huge amounts of loess, a fine yellow-brown silt, which colours the water.

questions.question: Which strait separates Spain from Morocco at the entrance to the Mediterranean?
questions.explanation: At its narrowest the Strait of Gibraltar is about 14 km wide.

questions.question: The Panama Canal connects which two oceans?
questions.explanation: The canal opened in 1914 and shortcuts the long route around South America.

questions.question: Which of these countries has a coast on the Caspian Sea?
questions.explanation: Uzbekistan lies inland, near the Aral Sea.

questions.question: About how long is the Suez Canal?
questions.explanation: The canal runs about 193 km between Port Said and Suez.

questions.question: About how big is the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explanation: The Mediterranean covers about 2.5 million km².

questions.question: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between Dover and Calais, is about how wide?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Dover is about 33 km across.

questions.question: In which city did the world's first underground railway open, in 1863?
questions.explanation: The Metropolitan Railway opened in London in January 1863.

questions.question: Which Great Lake lies entirely inside the United States?
questions.explanation: Lake Michigan is the only Great Lake wholly within US borders; the other four are shared with Canada.

questions.question: How many US states border Mexico?
questions.explanation: California, Arizona, New Mexico and Texas border Mexico.

questions.question: Which US state shares a land border with exactly one other US state?
questions.explanation: Maine borders only New Hampshire; Vermont has three neighbouring states, Rhode Island two and Delaware three.

questions.question: Vesuvius overlooks which Italian bay?
questions.explanation: Vesuvius rises above the Bay of Naples.

questions.question: About how many people died in the 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens?
questions.explanation: The eruption killed 57 people.

questions.question: About how long are the Ural Mountains?
questions.explanation: The Urals stretch about 2,500 kilometres from north to south.

questions.question: About how long are the Rocky Mountains?
questions.explanation: The Rockies stretch about 4,800 kilometres.

questions.question: About how tall is the Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world?
questions.explanation: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai stands about 828 metres tall.

questions.question: The Congo is the world's deepest river, reaching about how deep?
questions.explanation: Parts of the Congo are more than 220 m deep.

questions.question: The Great Rift Valley stretches about how far, from Jordan to Mozambique?
questions.explanation: The Rift system runs for roughly 6,000 km.

questions.question: About how large is the Amazon basin?
questions.explanation: The Amazon drains about 7 million km², nearly the size of Australia.

questions.question: At about what altitude does Lake Titicaca lie?
questions.explanation: The surface of Lake Titicaca is at about 3,812 m.

questions.question: About how high is Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest mountain?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro's Uhuru Peak stands at about 5,895 metres.

questions.question: How many countries and territories share the Amazon rainforest?
questions.explanation: Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Bolivia, Ecuador, Venezuela, Guyana, Suriname and French Guiana share it.

questions.question: About how deep is the deepest part of the Congo River?
questions.explanation: The Congo is the deepest river on record, at more than 220 metres in places.

questions.question: Which is the smallest country in Africa by area?
questions.explanation: Seychelles covers about 450 km².

questions.question: About how big is the Sahara Desert?
questions.explanation: The Sahara covers about 9 million km², close to the size of the United States.

questions.question: Which African country ranks second by area, just behind Algeria?
questions.explanation: The DR Congo covers about 2.34 million km², a little less than Algeria's 2.38 million.

questions.question: The Mekong flows through or along the borders of how many countries?
questions.explanation: China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam.

questions.question: About how long is the Yangtze, Asia's longest river?
questions.explanation: The Yangtze is roughly 6,300 km long.

questions.question: The Ganges and the Brahmaputra build the world's largest delta, shared by which two countries?
questions.explanation: Their delta, with the Sundarbans, spreads over India and Bangladesh.

questions.question: How many mountains on Earth rise above 8,000 metres?
questions.explanation: There are 14 eight-thousanders, all in Asia.

questions.question: Japan is made up of about how many islands?
questions.explanation: Japan counts more than 6,800 islands, most of them tiny.

questions.question: Indonesia stretches about how far from west to east?
questions.explanation: The archipelago spans roughly 5,100 km.

questions.question: About how high does Uluru rise above the surrounding plain?
questions.explanation: Uluru stands about 348 m above the plain.

questions.question: About how wide is the Cook Strait at its narrowest, between New Zealand's two main islands?
questions.explanation: At its narrowest the Cook Strait is about 22 km wide.

questions.question: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
questions.explanation: The capital was renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019 and returned to the name Astana in 2022.

questions.question: In which country is the historic city of Timbuktu?
questions.explanation: Timbuktu, a medieval centre of trade and learning, lies in Mali.

questions.question: About how high above sea level does the city centre of La Paz stand?
questions.explanation: La Paz sits at about 3,600 metres in the Andes, higher than any other large capital.

questions.question: The fixed link between Copenhagen and Malmö, the Øresund bridge and tunnel, is roughly how long?
questions.explanation: The Øresund fixed link is about 16 kilometres, partly bridge, partly an artificial island and partly a tunnel.

questions.question: Which national capital lies about 28 m below sea level, the lowest-lying in the world?
questions.explanation: Baku stands on the Caspian shore, which is itself about 28 metres below sea level.

questions.question: Counting only the city proper, which is the most populous city in the European Union?
questions.explanation: Within its city limits Berlin has about 3.7 million people, ahead of Madrid, Rome and Paris. Paris has the biggest metropolitan area of those.

questions.question: What is the officially recognised record for Earth's hottest air temperature?
questions.explanation: The World Meteorological Organization recognises 56.7 °C at Furnace Creek in Death Valley, recorded in July 1913.

questions.question: What is the lowest air temperature ever recorded on Earth?
questions.explanation: Vostok Station in Antarctica recorded about 89 degrees below zero Celsius on 21 July 1983.

questions.question: How many main climate groups does the Köppen system use?
questions.explanation: The five Köppen groups are A (tropical), B (dry), C (temperate), D (continental) and E (polar).

questions.question: The trade winds of the northern tropics blow mainly from which direction?
questions.explanation: In the northern tropics the trade winds blow from the north-east, and from the south-east south of the Equator.

questions.question: Between roughly which latitudes do the Roaring Forties blow?
questions.explanation: They are strong westerly winds over the southern oceans, between about 40° and 50° south.

questions.question: Oymyakon in Siberia recorded about what temperature in 1933, the lowest for a permanently inhabited place?
questions.explanation: The official record of about 68 degrees below zero Celsius was set at Oymyakon in 1933.

questions.question: Which continent ranks fifth in area, ahead of Europe and Oceania?
questions.explanation: By area the order is Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Oceania.

questions.question: Africa covers about what share of Earth's land area?
questions.explanation: Africa's roughly 30 million km² is about a fifth of the world's land.

questions.question: How many sovereign countries are in South America?
questions.explanation: The twelve are Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, Uruguay and Venezuela.

questions.question: Which of these countries lies partly in Africa and partly in Asia?
questions.explanation: Egypt's Sinai Peninsula is in Asia, while the rest of the country is in Africa.

questions.question: Which large Pacific island is divided between Indonesia and Papua New Guinea?
questions.explanation: The western half is Indonesian and the eastern half is the country of Papua New Guinea.

questions.question: About how high is Aconcagua, the highest mountain outside Asia?
questions.explanation: Aconcagua in Argentina rises to about 6,960 metres.

questions.question: Which two countries share the longest international land border in the world?
questions.explanation: The Canada–US border runs for roughly 8,900 km including the Alaska segment.

questions.question: The tallest dunes of the Namib Desert reach about how high?
questions.explanation: The huge red dunes of Sossusvlei in the Namib rise to roughly 300 metres, among the tallest on Earth.

questions.question: The Rub' al Khali, the world's largest continuous sand desert, covers about how much?
questions.explanation: The Rub' al Khali covers roughly 650,000 km², an area larger than France.

questions.question: The Gobi Desert covers roughly how much area?
questions.explanation: The Gobi covers about 1.3 million km² of Mongolia and northern China.

questions.question: About what share of Australia is arid or semi-arid?
questions.explanation: Roughly 70% of Australia gets little rain, which is why most people live near the coast.

questions.question: Antarctica, the world's largest desert, covers about how much?
questions.explanation: Antarctica covers roughly 14 million km² and is extremely dry as well as cold.

questions.question: Roughly what share of Earth's water is fresh rather than salt?
questions.explanation: About 97.5% of the water is salty, and most fresh water is locked in ice.

questions.question: Earth's mean radius is closest to which value?
questions.explanation: The average radius of the Earth is about 6,371 kilometres.

questions.question: Which is the largest tectonic plate?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Plate covers about 100 million km².

questions.question: If Mount Everest were placed in the Challenger Deep, its summit would lie about how far below the surface?
choices: It would stick out above the water
questions.explanation: Challenger Deep is about 10,900 metres deep and Everest about 8,850 metres high, leaving roughly 2 kilometres of water above the summit.

questions.question: Pangaea began to break apart about how long ago?
questions.explanation: The supercontinent started to split in the early Jurassic, around 200 million years ago.

questions.question: About how long is the Danube, Europe's second-longest river?
questions.explanation: The Danube is roughly 2,850 km long, after the Volga.

questions.question: The Alps stretch across how many countries?
questions.explanation: Austria, France, Germany, Italy, Liechtenstein, Monaco, Slovenia and Switzerland share the Alps.

questions.question: About how high is Aneto, the highest peak of the Pyrenees?
questions.explanation: Aneto reaches 3,404 m, far below Mont Blanc in the Alps.

questions.question: About how deep is the Baltic Sea on average?
questions.explanation: The Baltic is one of the shallowest seas: its average depth is about 55 m.

questions.question: About how large is the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explanation: The Mediterranean covers roughly 2.5 million km².

questions.question: About how large is Monaco, the second-smallest country in the world?
questions.explanation: Monaco covers about 2 km²; only Vatican City is smaller.

questions.question: About how long is the coastline of Greece, islands included?
questions.explanation: Thousands of islands give Greece a coastline of roughly 13,700 km.

questions.question: About what share of Iceland is covered by glaciers?
questions.explanation: Glaciers cover roughly a ninth of Iceland, around 11% of the island.

questions.question: The Qattara Depression, the lowest point of Egypt, lies about how far below sea level?
questions.explanation: The Qattara Depression reaches about 133 metres below sea level.

questions.question: About how often does Lake Eyre fill completely?
choices: Only a few times a century
questions.explanation: Lake Eyre is usually a dry salt pan and fills completely only a few times a century.

questions.question: Like Kilimanjaro, Puncak Jaya has what, despite lying close to the Equator?
questions.explanation: Puncak Jaya is one of the few tropical mountains with glaciers, though they are shrinking fast.

questions.question: About how big is Manitoulin Island?
questions.explanation: Manitoulin Island covers about 2,800 km² in Lake Huron.

questions.question: Honshu holds about what share of Japan's land area?
questions.explanation: Honshu covers about 228,000 km² of Japan's roughly 378,000 km².

questions.question: About how many islands are there in the Pacific Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Pacific has roughly 25,000 islands, more than all the other oceans combined.

questions.question: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal in Russia reaches about 1,642 metres deep.

questions.question: Which Great Lake lies entirely within the United States?
questions.explanation: The others are shared with Canada.

questions.question: About how long is Lake Malawi?
questions.explanation: Lake Malawi stretches about 580 km from north to south.

questions.question: Lesotho's lowest point is about how high above sea level, the highest lowest point of any country?
questions.explanation: Lesotho's lowest point, about 1,400 m, is higher than the lowest point of any other country.

questions.question: Ceuta and Melilla give the European Union its only land border with which continent?
questions.explanation: Both Spanish cities sit on the Moroccan coast, which gives the European Union its only land border with Africa.

questions.question: Cabinda lies just north of the mouth of which river?
questions.explanation: Cabinda is north of the Congo River's mouth, cut off from Angola by a strip of DR Congo.

questions.question: Which of these African countries does the Equator cross?
questions.explanation: The Equator crosses Gabon, the Republic of the Congo, the DR Congo, Uganda, Kenya and Somalia.

questions.question: You cross the International Date Line heading west. What happens to the calendar date?
questions.explanation: Going west across the line you skip ahead a calendar day; going east you repeat a day.

questions.question: Which city hosted the 1884 conference that chose Greenwich as the world's prime meridian?
questions.explanation: The International Meridian Conference met in Washington, D.C. and chose Greenwich.

questions.question: At the North Pole, the Sun stays above the horizon for about how long each year?
questions.explanation: The Sun rises once, around the March equinox, and sets around the September equinox.

questions.question: About what share of Earth's land lies in the Northern Hemisphere?
questions.explanation: The Northern Hemisphere holds roughly two thirds of the world's land.

questions.question: One degree of latitude spans about how far on the ground?
questions.explanation: Earth's circumference is about 40,000 km, so one degree out of 360 is roughly 111 km.

questions.question: Each standard time zone covers about how many degrees of longitude?
questions.explanation: 360 degrees divided by 24 hours gives 15 degrees per hour.

questions.question: Contour lines are drawn every 20 m. A hiker climbs from the 400 m line to the 560 m line. How many lines does she cross after the 400 m one, up to and including the 560 m one?
questions.explanation: From 420 to 560 in steps of 20 there are eight lines.

questions.question: On a map at 1:50,000, how many kilometres do 4 cm on the map stand for?
questions.explanation: 4 cm times 50,000 is 200,000 cm, which is 2 km.

questions.question: About how long is the Earth's mean radius?
questions.explanation: The mean radius is about 6,371 km.

questions.question: Which is the second-highest mountain on Earth?
questions.explanation: K2 rises to about 8,611 metres on the border of Pakistan and China.

questions.question: About how long is Monaco's land border with France?
questions.explanation: Monaco's whole land border is about 4.4 km.

questions.question: Which two countries share the record for the most land neighbours, with 14 each?
questions.explanation: China and Russia each border 14 countries; Brazil borders 10 and Germany 9.

questions.question: The Challenger Deep, at about 10.9 km, is roughly how many times deeper than the average ocean depth of about 3.7 km?
questions.explanation: Dividing 10.9 by 3.7 gives about 3: the deepest point is roughly three times the average depth.

questions.question: About how deep is the Tonga Trench at its deepest point?
questions.explanation: The Horizon Deep in the Tonga Trench reaches about 10,800 m, the deepest point in the Southern Hemisphere.

questions.question: About how much water do all the world's oceans hold?
questions.explanation: The oceans hold about 1.3 billion cubic kilometres of water.

questions.question: The Antarctic Circumpolar Current carries roughly how much water every second?
questions.explanation: Its flow of roughly 100 to 150 million cubic metres per second is several times that of the Gulf Stream.

questions.question: El Niño is a periodic warming of surface waters in which ocean?
questions.explanation: It occurs in the equatorial Pacific and affects weather worldwide.

questions.question: About how high is Aconcagua?
questions.explanation: Aconcagua rises to about 6,960 metres.

questions.question: About how high is Mount Elbrus?
questions.explanation: Elbrus rises to about 5,640 metres, well above Mont Blanc at about 4,810 metres.

questions.question: Vinson Massif is part of which mountain range?
questions.explanation: Vinson Massif is in the Sentinel Range of the Ellsworth Mountains.

questions.question: What share of the world's people live in cities today?
questions.explanation: About 57% of the world's population is urban.

questions.question: About how many languages are spoken in the world today?
questions.explanation: Linguists count roughly 7,000 living languages.

questions.question: About what is the median age of the world's population?
questions.explanation: Half of humanity is younger than about 30.

questions.question: Greater Tokyo is home to roughly how many people?
questions.explanation: The Tokyo area has more than 30 million inhabitants.

questions.question: About what share of the Earth's land does Asia cover?
questions.explanation: Asia covers roughly 30% of the world's land.

questions.question: Which is the deepest lake in Africa?
questions.explanation: Lake Tanganyika is about 1,470 metres deep.

questions.question: The Antarctic ice sheet is on average about how thick?
questions.explanation: The ice averages about 2 kilometres thick and is over 4 kilometres thick in places.

questions.question: If the whole Greenland ice sheet melted, sea level would rise by about how much?
questions.explanation: The Greenland ice sheet holds enough water to raise global sea level by roughly 7 metres.

questions.question: Between roughly which latitudes does the Svalbard archipelago lie?
questions.explanation: Svalbard lies far north of the Arctic Circle, between about 74° and 81° north.

questions.question: Magnetic declination is the angle between which two directions?
questions.explanation: Declination tells you how far a compass needle points away from true north.

questions.question: About what fraction of an iceberg's volume lies below the water?
questions.explanation: Ice is only slightly lighter than seawater, so roughly 90% of an iceberg is submerged.

questions.question: About how many people are in Antarctica at the busiest time of the summer?
questions.explanation: Around 5,000 researchers and staff are there in summer, and about 1,000 in winter.

questions.question: About how much water does the Amazon discharge into the Atlantic every second?
questions.explanation: Its average discharge is about 209,000 cubic metres per second.

questions.question: Ships in the Panama Canal are lifted by locks up to Gatún Lake. About how high above sea level is the lake?
questions.explanation: Gatún Lake sits about 26 m above sea level, so ships climb up and down through locks.

questions.question: At its narrowest the Bosphorus is about how wide?
questions.explanation: The strait narrows to roughly 700 m, which is why bridges can span it.

questions.question: About how long is the Strait of Malacca?
questions.explanation: It stretches roughly 800 km between the island of Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula.

questions.question: About how big is the Gulf of Mexico?
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Mexico covers about 1.55 million km² and is the largest gulf in the world.

questions.question: Big Diomede and Little Diomede, two islands in the Bering Strait, lie about how far apart?
questions.explanation: The islands are about 3.8 km apart. Big Diomede is Russian, Little Diomede is American, and the international date line runs between them.

questions.question: Which French-born engineer drew the plan of Washington, D.C. in 1791?
questions.explanation: Pierre Charles L'Enfant laid out the broad avenues and squares of the new federal city.

questions.question: Canberra's plan came from an international design competition won in which year?
questions.explanation: The American architect Walter Burley Griffin won the Canberra design competition in 1912.

questions.question: How many Indian states have Chandigarh as their capital?
questions.explanation: Chandigarh is the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana.

questions.question: Jericho has been settled for roughly how long, making it one of the oldest cities in the world?
questions.explanation: Jericho has traces of settlement from around 9000 BC, more than 11,000 years ago.

questions.question: Which is the largest city in the world north of the Arctic Circle?
questions.explanation: Murmansk, a Russian port that stays ice-free, has around 270,000 inhabitants.

questions.question: Which Argentine city on Tierra del Fuego is often called the southernmost city in the world?
questions.explanation: Ushuaia, at about 55 degrees south, is the usual answer, though some count Puerto Williams in Chile.

questions.question: About how many kilometres of canals does Amsterdam have?
questions.explanation: Amsterdam's network of canals totals roughly 100 kilometres.

questions.question: About how high is Denali, the highest peak in North America?
questions.explanation: Denali rises to about 6,190 metres (20,310 feet) in Alaska.

questions.question: Which US state contains both the highest point (Mount Whitney) and the lowest point (Badwater Basin) of the contiguous United States?
questions.explanation: Mount Whitney and Death Valley's Badwater Basin are in California, only about 135 km apart.

questions.question: The lowest point in North America, Badwater Basin, lies about how far below sea level?
questions.explanation: Badwater Basin is 282 feet, about 86 metres, below sea level.

questions.question: Which US state has the highest average elevation?
questions.explanation: Colorado's average elevation is about 2,070 metres. Alaska has the highest peak but much lower land on average.

questions.question: About how high above sea level is Mauna Kea, the highest point in Hawaii?
questions.explanation: Mauna Kea's summit is 4,207 metres above sea level.

questions.question: About how high is Guadalupe Peak, the highest point in Texas?
questions.explanation: Guadalupe Peak rises to 8,751 feet, about 2,667 metres.

questions.question: About what share of the world's surface fresh water do the Great Lakes hold?
questions.explanation: The Great Lakes hold roughly a fifth of the world's surface fresh water.

questions.question: About how long is the Rio Grande, which forms much of the border between Texas and Mexico?
questions.explanation: The Rio Grande is about 3,000 kilometres long, among the longest rivers of North America.

questions.question: In which year did Yellowstone become the world's first national park?
questions.explanation: The US Congress protected Yellowstone in 1872.

questions.question: Everglades National Park covers about how large an area?
questions.explanation: The park covers about 6,100 square kilometres, 1.5 million acres.

questions.question: About how tall is each face carved into Mount Rushmore?
questions.explanation: Each head is about 60 feet, roughly 18 metres, tall.

questions.question: About how deep is Crater Lake, the deepest lake in the United States?
questions.explanation: Crater Lake in Oregon, formed in a collapsed volcano, is about 594 metres (1,943 feet) deep.

questions.question: Which is the largest national park in the United States by area?
questions.explanation: Wrangell–St. Elias, in Alaska, covers more than 53,000 km².

questions.question: The United States has how many national parks, as of 2024?
questions.explanation: The National Park Service manages 63 national parks, among more than 400 protected areas.

questions.question: About how long is the mapped part of Mammoth Cave, the longest known cave system in the world?
questions.explanation: Mammoth Cave in Kentucky has more than 680 kilometres (over 420 miles) of surveyed passages.

questions.question: About how tall is General Sherman, the largest tree on Earth by volume?
questions.explanation: General Sherman, a giant sequoia, stands about 84 metres (275 feet) tall.

questions.question: At the Four Corners point, which four US states meet?
choices: Colorado, Utah, Arizona and New Mexico
Texas, Oklahoma, New Mexico and Colorado
questions.explanation: The Four Corners is the only point in the United States where four states meet: Colorado, Utah, Arizona and New Mexico.

questions.question: How many US states border the Great Lakes?
questions.explanation: Minnesota, Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania and New York all have Great Lakes shores.

questions.question: How many US states does the Mississippi River border or flow through?
questions.explanation: The Mississippi touches Minnesota, Wisconsin, Iowa, Illinois, Missouri, Kentucky, Tennessee, Arkansas, Mississippi and Louisiana.

questions.question: About how many times larger is Alaska than Texas by area?
questions.explanation: Alaska covers about 1.7 million square kilometres, about two and a half times Texas.

questions.question: Which two US states have borders made up only of straight lines of latitude and longitude, like rectangles?
questions.explanation: Colorado and Wyoming are the only two states whose borders are all straight lines.

questions.question: The 1815 eruption of which Indonesian volcano caused "the year without a summer" in 1816?
questions.explanation: Tambora's ash and gas cooled the climate and caused crop failures across the world in 1816.

questions.question: About how high is Mauna Loa above sea level?
questions.explanation: Mauna Loa rises about 4,170 metres above sea level.

questions.question: When did Yellowstone's most recent giant caldera eruption happen?
questions.explanation: The last giant eruption of the Yellowstone caldera was about 640,000 years ago.

questions.question: Angel Falls, the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, is in which country?
questions.explanation: Angel Falls drops 979 metres in Venezuela's Canaima National Park.

questions.question: About how much of the Channel Tunnel's length runs under the sea?
questions.explanation: About 38 km of its 50 km are under the Channel.

questions.question: The Burj Khalifa, completed in 2010, is about how tall?
questions.explanation: The Burj Khalifa is 828 m tall.

questions.question: About how long is the Great Barrier Reef?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef stretches about 2,300 km.

questions.question: About how long are all the sections of the Great Wall of China together?
questions.explanation: A survey found its walls, trenches and natural barriers total about 21,000 km.

questions.question: Among countries lying wholly in Europe, which is the largest landlocked one?
questions.explanation: Belarus covers about 208,000 km². Kazakhstan is larger but lies mostly in Asia.

questions.question: What is Europe's officially recognised record high temperature, set in 2021?
questions.explanation: The World Meteorological Organization recognised 48.8 °C in Sicily on 11 August 2021 as the European record.

questions.question: How wide is the Bering Strait at its narrowest?
questions.explanation: The strait between Russia and Alaska is about 80 km wide at its narrowest.

questions.question: Which country has the most time zones, counting its overseas territories?
questions.explanation: France spans about 12 or 13 time zones because of its overseas territories.

questions.question: The continental crust is on average about how thick?
questions.explanation: Continental crust averages roughly 30 to 40 kilometres, and is thickest under big mountain ranges.

questions.question: About how thick is Earth's mantle?
questions.explanation: The mantle extends from the crust down to about 2,900 kilometres deep.

questions.question: At the Equator, how fast does Earth's surface move because of its rotation?
questions.explanation: Going round the roughly 40,000 km Equator in about 24 hours means about 1,670 kilometres per hour.

questions.question: By about how much is the Dead Sea shoreline dropping each year?
questions.explanation: The Dead Sea level has been falling by roughly a metre a year.

questions.question: Which two countries border Russia's Kaliningrad region by land?
questions.explanation: The region is squeezed between Poland to the south and Lithuania to the north and east.

questions.question: Baarle-Hertog, the Belgian part of the town of Baarle, is made up of about how many separate pieces of land?
questions.explanation: Baarle-Hertog consists of about two dozen separate parcels, most of them enclaves inside the Netherlands.

questions.question: One degree of latitude is about how many kilometres?
questions.explanation: One degree of latitude spans about 111 km everywhere on Earth.

questions.question: One nautical mile equals exactly how many metres?
questions.explanation: A nautical mile is defined as 1,852 m.

questions.question: The shortest flight path from London to New York, along a great circle, is about how long?
questions.explanation: The great-circle distance is roughly 5,570 km.

questions.question: GPS satellites orbit at about what altitude?
questions.explanation: GPS satellites circle at about 20,200 km.

questions.question: Which mountain's summit is the farthest from the centre of the Earth?
questions.explanation: Earth bulges at the equator, so the summit of Chimborazo in Ecuador is farthest from the centre, though Everest is highest above sea level.
questions.misconception: Many people think Mount Everest is the tallest and the farthest-from-Earth's-centre mountain in every sense.

questions.question: About how long is the border between Chile and Argentina?
questions.explanation: The border follows the crest of the Andes for about 6,700 km.

questions.question: How many mountains on Earth are higher than 8,000 metres?
questions.explanation: There are fourteen "eight-thousanders", all in the Himalaya and the Karakoram.

questions.question: Roughly how many people per km² live in Monaco, the world's most densely populated country?
questions.explanation: Some 38,000 people live in about 2 km².

questions.question: As of 2023, how many official languages does South Africa recognise?
questions.explanation: South Africa has 12 official languages, including South African Sign Language since 2023.

questions.question: Which country has the fourth-largest population in the world?
questions.explanation: After India, China and the United States, Indonesia comes fourth.

questions.question: What is the average elevation of Antarctica, the highest continent?
questions.explanation: Thick ice on a land mass makes Antarctica the highest continent on average, at roughly 2,500 metres.

questions.question: The Ross Ice Shelf, Antarctica's largest, is about as big as which country?
questions.explanation: It covers roughly 490,000 km², comparable to France.

questions.question: Which river flows through more countries than any other in the world?
questions.explanation: The Danube flows through ten countries, from Germany to the Black Sea.

questions.question: Which US state has the lowest high point of all, only about 105 m above sea level?
questions.explanation: Britton Hill in Florida rises to 345 feet, about 105 metres, the lowest highest point of any state.

questions.question: Which is the highest peak in the United States east of the Mississippi River?
questions.explanation: Mount Mitchell in North Carolina, at 2,037 metres, edges out Clingmans Dome by only about 12 metres.

questions.question: Which two US states each border eight other states, more than any others?
questions.explanation: Tennessee and Missouri each border eight states.

questions.question: About how long is the global mid-ocean ridge system?
questions.explanation: The mid-ocean ridge system is about 65,000 km long, the longest mountain chain on Earth.

questions.question: The Gotthard Base Tunnel, the world's longest railway tunnel, is about how long?
questions.explanation: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is about 57 km long.

questions.question: The surveyed total length of all sections of the Great Wall of China is about...
questions.explanation: A 2012 Chinese survey of all walls from every dynasty gave about 21,000 km.

questions.question: The power capacity of the Three Gorges Dam is about...
questions.explanation: Its turbines can produce about 22.5 gigawatts.
